title: Monsoon and Summit
premise: Mirabel Ishikawa, a disgraced railroad engineer hiding in the mountain districts under a borrowed name, is hired to survey closed rail lines when he stumbles on the abandoned camp of a vanished government survey team. Following the river upstream toward its forbidden source, he uncovers that the team was silenced after finding evidence of a falsified land grant—one that would displace an entire valley's people before the monsoon floods it. Hunted by the officials who erased the surveyors, torn between the loyalty he owes his old mentor (who signed the falsification) and the truth he owes the dead, Mirabel must choose justice outside the law: he delivers the evidence to the valley elders and detonates the old line's last bridge to stop the government crews, ending the book standing at the river's source as the monsoon finally breaks—his real name spoken aloud for the first time in years.
about_author: G. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former civil engineer who spent a decade mapping remote rail corridors across monsoon country before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for technical precision, moral ambiguity, and landscapes that behave like characters.

chapters.title: The Man with Two Names
chapters.summary: Mirabel Ishikawa arrives in the mountain junction town of Kellwater under a false name, taking a low-paying contract to survey decommissioned rail lines. His POV establishes his debt, his compass inherited from his father, and his careful invisibility. Emotional beat: weary self-erasure, the ache of a man who has decided being nobody is safety.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Surveying a tunnel sealed years ago, Mirabel finds fresh tool marks inside—someone reopened it recently. He says nothing to his employer, the district land office. His POV; beat: first crack in his anonymity, curiosity overriding caution, and a flicker of the engineer's pride he thought buried.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Two days upstream, Mirabel finds the government survey team's camp: instruments laid out neatly, a cold stove, no bodies, no tracks leading out. Only boot prints arriving. His POV; beat: dread blooming into obsession—the neatness of the abandonment is worse than violence would be.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Back in Kellwater, innkeeper Sera Oduya notices Mirabel's shaken state and trades him soup for fragments of the story. Her POV reveals the town's quiet resentments toward the land office. Beat: warmth and suspicion entwined; Mirabel realizes people here watch everything.

chapters.title: A Compass Points Nowhere
chapters.summary: Mirabel discovers the survey team's field journal hidden in the tunnel, its final pages torn out, and a compass bearing pointing upriver toward the forbidden source valley. His POV; beat: the pull of the unfinished—every instinct to flee wars with the need to know what page was torn away.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Signature
chapters.summary: In the district archive, Mirabel finds a land grant bearing his old mentor Aldous Vane's signature—Vane, who taught him everything, certifying a flood scheme for the source valley. His POV; beat: betrayal's cold arrival, loyalty and truth beginning their war.

chapters.title: Men from the Land Office
chapters.summary: Two officials arrive in Kellwater asking about a 'stray surveyor,' showing a sketch that is unmistakably Mirabel's face. Sera lies for him without being asked. Her POV; beat: the terrifying discovery that someone else has decided his life matters.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Mirabel burns his contract papers and follows the river into the gorge, using the dead team's compass bearing. His POV; beat: liberation and terror together—he has chosen motion over hiding, and there is no path back down.

chapters.title: The Drowned Tunnel
chapters.summary: A spring flood traps Mirabel in a half-submerged bore where he finds one of the missing surveyors, alive but broken-legged: junior engineer Tomas Reyes. Alternating POV; beat: relief curdling into fear—Reyes whispers that the others were taken, not lost.

chapters.title: What Reyes Saw
chapters.summary: Reyes recounts how the team found pre-flood ruins and a forged boundary stone proving the grant was backdated; the crew chief was arrested by their own escort. Reyes's POV; beat: guilt and survival shame, and the torn pages' location revealed—the chief swallowed the key detail, but Reyes memorized the coordinates.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Forecast
chapters.summary: Carrying Reyes on a litter, Mirabel calculates the storm front's landfall against their pace: eleven days. The land office men are behind them, moving faster. His POV; beat: the race made concrete—numbers, weather, and pursuit compressed into a single countdown.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: Cut to Kellwater: Sera is detained for questioning and realizes the officials intend to make her disappearance permanent. She escapes with the town's tacit help and heads upriver after Mirabel. Her POV; beat: courage she never claimed, loyalty becoming action.

chapters.title: The Valley That Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel reaches the source valley's edge and meets the elder Nadya Kesh, who shows him ruins older than any grant—and reveals her people have been quietly moving stones off the boundary markers for generations. Nadya's POV; beat: dignity under erasure; Mirabel sees what the paper crime would actually drown.

chapters.title: Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Guided by Reyes's memorized coordinates, Mirabel recovers the journal's torn pages cached in a shrine above the gorge: Vane's own annotations admitting the forgery, kept as blackmail by the crew chief. His POV; beat: vindication without comfort—proof in hand means he can no longer pretend neutrality.

chapters.title: The Escort Returns
chapters.summary: The land office men catch them at the shrine; Reyes is taken, and Mirabel escapes with the pages only because Nadya's people stage a rockslide. His POV; beat: failure's cost—survival purchased with another man's capture, and rage hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Letter to a Ghost
chapters.summary: Mirabel writes to Vane offering him the chance to confess publicly before Mirabel delivers the pages to the valley council. A reply comes: come to the old line's last bridge, alone. His POV; beat: hope and trap indistinguishable—the mentor's voice still able to move him like weather.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Kilometer Forty
chapters.summary: At the condemned trestle, Vane admits the forgery but argues the flood scheme will save ten thousand downstream lives—a utilitarian sin. Sera arrives mid-confrontation; the land office men close in. Vane's POV; beat: the mentor's tragedy revealed—he believes his own arithmetic, and begs Mirabel to stay invisible.

chapters.title: Demolition Charge
chapters.summary: Cornered, Mirabel uses his engineer's knowledge to drop the trestle with its own decayed piers, stranding the officials' convoy and destroying the access route for the flood crews. His POV; beat: climax—justice outside the law, chosen fully, his old life blown apart with the span.

chapters.title: Testimony at the Source
chapters.summary: Before the assembled valley council, Mirabel speaks his true name aloud for the first time in years and delivers the pages; Nadya's people seal copies in three places so no single arrest can erase them. Council scene, rotating POV; beat: truth made durable—no longer one man's burden but a community's record.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: News arrives that Vane has confessed publicly and been arrested, naming Mirabel as his witness—an act that shields Mirabel legally but costs Vane everything. Sera's POV; beat: grief braided with gratitude; loyalty and truth reconciled at terrible price.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits as the valley completes its defenses; the flood comes and stops exactly where the old boundary stone stands. Mirabel, Reyes, and Sera watch the water hold the line. His POV; beat: catharsis—the storm he raced arrives and loses.

chapters.title: Monsoon and Summit
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Mirabel signs a new survey contract—not to hide, but to map the valley's future rail spur openly, compass in hand, debt paid. Final image: climbing toward the river's source in clear post-storm light. His POV; beat: resolution—identity reclaimed not as escape from the past but as authorship of what comes next.
